reason: The cited evidence shows active learning reduces DFT calculations and achieves DFT accuracy for properties like solid solution strengthening in multicomponent alloys (E1), and that MLIPs can be trained on ab initio data (E2), but neither passage addresses fusion, free energies, vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, or electron-vibration coupling, leaving the core premises about phase-transition thermodynamics unsupported.
premises: Active learning can automatically generate MLIP training sets tailored to a system with minimal DFT calculations
MLIPs trained on ab initio data can achieve DFT accuracy for material properties
Active learning reduces computational cost by focusing DFT evaluations on high-uncertainty regions
MLIPs enable larger supercells and better configurational averaging than traditional methods
The approach is applicable to elemental/binary systems near fusion where vibrational entropy and anharmonicity matter
